title: Build a min-heap priority queue in Python using heapq
description: Greenfield Python task: implement a MinPQ class wrapping heapq with push, pop, peek, is_empty, and __len__ operations.

injections.content:
import pytest
from src.minpq import MinPQ


def test_empty_initially():
    pq = MinPQ()
    assert pq.is_empty()
    assert len(pq) == 0


def test_push_and_pop_order():
    pq = MinPQ()
    pq.push(5)
    pq.push(1)
    pq.push(3)
    assert pq.pop() == 1
    assert pq.pop() == 3
    assert pq.pop() == 5


def test_peek_does_not_remove():
    pq = MinPQ()
    pq.push(7)
    pq.push(2)
    assert pq.peek() == 2
    assert len(pq) == 2


def test_len_tracks_operations():
    pq = MinPQ()
    pq.push(10)
    pq.push(20)
    assert len(pq) == 2
    pq.pop()
    assert len(pq) == 1


def test_pop_empty_raises():
    pq = MinPQ()
    with pytest.raises(IndexError):
        pq.pop()


def test_peek_empty_raises():
    pq = MinPQ()
    with pytest.raises(IndexError):
        pq.peek()


def test_is_empty_after_all_pops():
    pq = MinPQ()
    pq.push(42)
    pq.pop()
    assert pq.is_empty()

required_artifacts: pop returns elements in ascending order
peek does not remove the minimum element
pop and peek raise IndexError when empty
